positions.commentary: The speaker highlights META's accelerating revenue growth for the third consecutive quarter, indicating a strong recovery.
The speaker views Constellation Software positively, noting its low valuation relative to its significant growth in free cash flow.

thesis: The episode argues that Meta is the primary beneficiary of AI, converting advancements into accelerating revenue growth and strong operational metrics despite high capital expenditures. While the speaker notes the necessity of significant CAPEX, they maintain a bullish view on Meta's recovery and valuation, whereas LVMH is viewed as neutral and Constellation Software is highlighted for its low valuation relative to free cash flow growth.

claims.claim: Louis Vuitton is considered a durable business with no AI risk.
claims.quote: Plus the fact that these do tend to be pretty durable businesses, definitely not an AI risk in Louis Vuitton and Tiffany.

claims.claim: The speaker describes LVMH as having nothing earth shattering going on.
claims.quote: So that's kind of LVMH and a nutshell, nothing earth shattering going on there.

claims.claim: Meta is seen as a beneficiary of AI driving revenue growth, but its earnings are not fully reflective of underlying owner earnings due to high CapEx.
claims.quote: I'm not saying that's a bad thing. I'm not saying it can't be a good ROI. I'm just saying that counting numbers you're looking at are not fully reflective of the underlying owner, earnings, and the business.

claims.claim: Meta is the biggest beneficiary of AI today and turning advancements into actual revenue growth.
claims.quote: Now they're offsetting that by growing a lot, and I think they're going to continue to grow because almost more so than any other business, they seem to be the biggest beneficiary of AI today and actually turning a lot of these advancements into actual revenue growth.

claims.claim: Meta has been phenomenal with AI advancements like better algorithms and new ad attribution models driving growth.
claims.quote: There's all sorts of different things they called out on the call. Watchtime on Instagram, Reels is up 30% year-to-year in the United States. A lot of that's on a better algorithm.

claims.claim: Facebook optimizations resulted in a 7% lift in organic feed and video post.
claims.quote: Facebook optimizations resulted in a 7% lift in organic feed and video post.

claims.claim: A new ad attribution model drove a 24% increase in incremental conversion versus the standard model.
claims.quote: A new ad attribution model, 24% increase in incremental conversion versus the standard model, okay.

claims.claim: The core business is performing exceptionally well, supported by significant AI-driven growth in watchtime, ad optimization, and conversion, despite high capital expenditures.
claims.quote: Everything is going really, really well for them. They maybe are making some questionable capital allocation decisions. We won't know until after the fact. But the core business is doing really well and kind of supports a lot of these activities too.

claims.claim: META is a major beneficiary of AI, converting advancements into revenue growth, with specific metrics showing substantial year-to-year increases in watchtime and ad performance.
claims.quote: Now they're offsetting that by growing a lot, and I think they're going to continue to grow because almost more so than any other business, they seem to be the biggest beneficiary of AI today and actually turning a lot of these advancements into actual revenue growth. And it's been phenomenal for them.

claims.claim: Even if META does not achieve the best AI models, they are still generating returns on their ad spend and can utilize data centers for existing models.
claims.quote: It seems like even if they don't get, you know, the best sort of model, they're still getting some sort of return on this ad spend. claims.claim: META's top line is growing at 20 percent plus, and adjusting for Reality Labs losses brings the valuation multiple closer to 23 times.
claims.quote: If you're pulling out the reality labs losses, then you're getting closer to a 23 times multiple for a company that is growing top line, you know, 20 percent plus.

claims.claim: META is expected to see a big acceleration of AI next year, leading to rapid gains even if they are not on the leading edge.
claims.quote: Even if they're not in the leading edge, the sort of gains that they'll be making will be showing up a lot in the distance will be cut very rapidly.

claims.claim: The speaker questions whether META needed to spend $72 billion in CAPEX last year to achieve their results, suggesting they might have achieved similar results with less spending.
claims.quote: Now, again, the question is did they need to spend the 72 billion in CAPEX last year to get these results? Could they have done it with 40 maybe? And I'm not saying they shouldn't have spent the 72 to continue to grow.

claims.claim: The speaker views Constellation Software positively, noting its low valuation relative to its significant growth in free cash flow.
claims.quote: But right now, as we speak, Constellation, you know, the US ticker, CNSFW, is trading at around 17 times free cash flow. And so it's interesting because it's not quite, but almost back to the spot where it was at when we originally wrote about it three years ago. And free cash flow has actually grown over 150% since then.
